explanation:
[EFFECT] The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic, bimodal effect on predicted demand. Contributions are most negative during the early morning hours (roughly midnight to 5 AM, with the deepest trough around 4 AM), meaning these hours strongly suppress rentals. Demand rises sharply from about 5 AM onward, reaching a first peak at around 8 AM (morning commute) and a slightly higher second peak at around 5 PM (evening commute, the overall highest point in the plot), before declining again through the late evening.

[IMPORTANCE] Hour of the day is the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st out of 9, with an importance score of 0.833 — far higher than any other feature. It is the dominant driver of hourly bike demand predictions.

[RECOMMENDATION] Bike availability and staff should be concentrated around the 8 AM and 5 PM commuter peaks, and significantly reduced during the overnight hours (midnight to 5 AM), when demand is consistently at its lowest.
